schema_note: Static, VibePromptRig-curated catalog read by the /vibepromptrig:setup skill. NOT a live registry -- updated only when the plugin is rebuilt + published. For anything this catalog misses, /setup directs the user to /vibepromptrig:mcp-advisor (live registry search). See docs/architecture/equip-discovery.md.
disclaimer: VibePromptRig /setup recommendations are best-effort. Verify any MCP server before installing, especially those with network, filesystem-write, or secrets-access permissions. The full install command is shown before you approve. You are responsible for what runs in your Claude Code session. 'publisher_verified' is set only by the project owner after a personal vetting pass -- 'verified_against' + 'last_vetted' record only that the install command matched the named source on that date.

field_reference.stack_triggers: Signals in the scanned project that make this entry relevant. type: package (string match inside a manifest file) | dir (directory name present) | file (file present) | dep-any (any of several deps).
field_reference.confidence: high | medium | low -- drives proposal ordering (max 5 per run, highest first).
field_reference.known_permissions: network | filesystem-read | filesystem-write | secrets-access -- shown to the user before approval.
field_reference.publisher_verified: boolean -- publisher-only personal vouch. false does NOT mean unsafe; it means not-yet-personally-vetted.
field_reference.verified_against: What source the install command was checked against, and 'last_vetted' when.
field_reference.sha256: Tarball checksum when the entry pins a fixed artifact. null for npx packages and hosted HTTP servers.
field_reference.launcher_pins: Every npx package in install.command is pinned to an exact version (the version npm published as latest on 2026-09-25): mcp-remote@0.14.3. Pinning keeps what /setup writes reproducible; bump each pin deliberately after checking the package release notes. The pin was chosen on 2026-09-25 without re-vetting; last_vetted still refers to the earlier check of the command shape, and the entry's verified_against records the 2026-09-25 recheck. Stripe and Supabase moved to their hosted HTTP servers on 2026-09-27 and no longer use a launcher.
field_reference.tombstoned: true = a previously-shipped entry marked insecure/retired. /setup NEVER proposes a tombstoned entry, and warns if one is already installed.

entries.name: Supabase MCP
entries.plain_summary: Let Claude inspect the development database you choose, using read-only access.
entries.plain_access: Can read information in the selected development database and connect to Supabase online. Cannot change the database with this read-only configuration. Private information may be visible.
entries.plain_account: A Supabase account; sign in through your browser when you first use the connection.
entries.plain_when: Useful only if your app stores information in Supabase and you choose help with storing information.
entries.summary: Hosted Supabase MCP, read-only and scoped to the selected development project; inspect data and schema without write access.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project uses Supabase (detected @supabase/supabase-js and/or a supabase/ directory).

install.requires: Browser OAuth on first use (type /mcp in Claude Code to authenticate). No token to store. Replace <your-dev-project-ref> with your DEV project's ref, never production.

entries.verified_against: official Supabase MCP docs: hosted server https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp, configured by the project_ref and read_only URL parameters, OAuth by default (docs read 2026-09-26; command changed to this form 2026-09-27). Not vetted: this command has not been connected to a real project; last_vetted refers to the earlier npx command.
entries.notes: Read-only and scoped to your DEV project through the URL (read_only=true, project_ref), never prod -- per data-protection.md token-scope tiers. Remove read_only=true only when you explicitly intend migrations. The docs' personal-access-token header is a fallback for clients without OAuth; it grants more than OAuth scope, so /setup does not propose it.

entries.name: Vercel MCP
entries.plain_summary: Help Claude find information about your Vercel-hosted website and its deployments.
entries.plain_access: Can access the deployment information, logs and project details your sign-in allows. This configuration does not enforce read-only access; review available actions before use.
entries.plain_account: A Vercel account; sign in through your browser when you first use the connection.
entries.plain_when: Useful only if you use Vercel to put your app online and choose help with hosting.
entries.summary: Official hosted Vercel MCP -- gives Claude OAuth access to your deployments, logs, project metadata, and Vercel docs.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project deploys on Vercel (detected vercel.json, a .vercel/ directory, or Next.js).

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http vercel https://mcp.vercel.com
install.requires: Browser OAuth on first use (type /mcp in Claude Code to authenticate). No token to store.

entries.notes: Hosted + OAuth -- no secret lands in .mcp.json. Read-leaning by design.

entries.name: GitHub MCP
entries.plain_summary: Let Claude work with the code, issues and reviews you permit in GitHub.
entries.plain_access: Can read or change the repositories and other GitHub information allowed by your access key. It may start paid automatic checks if that key permits it.
entries.plain_account: A GitHub account and a narrowly limited access key. Set the key locally; never paste it into this conversation. Skip this connection if the key is not ready.
entries.plain_when: Useful only if you use GitHub and choose help with checking work automatically.
entries.summary: GitHub's official remote MCP -- repos, issues, PRs, code search, Actions.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project has a GitHub remote (detected github.com in .git/config).

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_GITHUB_PAT>"
install.requires: A GitHub Personal Access Token. Grant only the scopes you are comfortable giving an AI tool.

entries.notes: The PAT is the whole blast radius -- scope it minimally (read-only where possible). On CLI 2.1.1+ you can use `claude mcp add-json github ...` instead. Claude Desktop needs the local Docker setup (OAuth app not supported there).

entries.name: Cloudflare Docs MCP
entries.plain_summary: Help Claude search instructions for using Cloudflare services.
entries.plain_access: Reads public Cloudflare documentation online. Starts a local helper to make that connection; this option does not grant access to manage your Cloudflare account.
entries.plain_account: No Cloudflare sign-in is needed for this public documentation connection.
entries.plain_when: Useful only if your app uses Cloudflare and you choose help with putting it online.
entries.summary: Cloudflare's hosted documentation MCP -- searchable Workers/Pages/D1/R2/KV docs in-session.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project targets Cloudflare (detected wrangler.toml / wrangler.jsonc / a Workers entrypoint).

install.requires: Nothing for the docs server (read-only). Cloudflare's account-scoped servers (Workers, D1, R2 admin) are separate and OAuth-gated -- add those deliberately.

entries.verified_against: official Cloudflare Agents docs (command matched on last_vetted). Recheck 2026-09-25, version pin not vetted: the docs now list https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp; /sse remains an alias.
entries.notes: This entry is the read-only DOCS server only. The account-management Cloudflare servers carry filesystem-write-equivalent authority over your CF account -- do not auto-add them; vet each separately.

entries.name: Stripe MCP
entries.plain_summary: Help Claude work with the Stripe payment information and actions you permit.
entries.plain_access: Can read or change payment information within the access you authorize. Choose a test environment while building; review its permissions before first use.
entries.plain_account: A Stripe account; sign in through your browser when you first use the connection.
entries.plain_when: Useful only if you use Stripe to accept payments and choose payment help.
entries.summary: Official Stripe MCP -- customers, subscriptions, invoices, product catalog, plus Stripe docs/knowledge-base search.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project integrates Stripe (detected the stripe dependency).

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/
install.requires: Browser OAuth on first use (type /mcp in Claude Code to authenticate). No key to store. Prefer authorizing a sandbox (test) environment while you build.

entries.verified_against: official Stripe MCP docs: hosted server https://mcp.stripe.com with OAuth (docs read 2026-09-26; command changed to this form 2026-09-27). From 2026-10-31 Stripe MCP rejects secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag; OAuth is unaffected. Not vetted: no live connection has been made with this command; last_vetted refers to the earlier npx command.
entries.notes: Money surface. OAuth keeps secrets out of .mcp.json, and access can be reviewed or revoked in the Stripe Dashboard. Unverified: for Connect platforms acting on connected accounts, Stripe's docs still describe a platform restricted key because OAuth is not supported there. Pair with the webhook-handling rule pack below.

entries.name: VibePromptRig pre-commit gates
entries.plain_summary: Add automated checks that can catch some secrets, unsafe changes and unsupported completion claims before you save a code change.
entries.plain_access: Runs local check programs before a code commit and may block it. Changes this project only; it does not replace checks you already customized.
entries.plain_account: No external account is needed; Git and the required local helper tools must be available.
entries.plain_when: Useful when this project uses Git to track changes and does not already have these checks.
entries.summary: Installs the factory's tracked git hooks (.githooks/ wired via core.hooksPath): secrets scan, architect-first gate on feat() commits, destructive-SQL block, user-facing component-deletion gate, discovery interlock.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project is a git repository without the VibePromptRig mechanical gates installed. The factory rules assume these gates exist -- per enforcement-first.md, a load-bearing rule without a mechanical gate WILL decay.
entries.notes: First-party. All gates are soft-with-override ([no-arch:], [approved-destructive], [approved-deletion], [discovery-skipped]) -- the marker IS the audit trail. Rollback: git config --unset core.hooksPath, then delete .githooks/. Never proposed/installed over an existing hooks setup (husky, custom core.hooksPath) -- merge manually in that case.

entries.name: Finance domain primer
entries.plain_summary: Give Claude instructions for handling money-related features carefully.
entries.plain_access: Adds a local reference document. It guides Claude; it does not itself change financial records or enforce an automated check.
entries.plain_account: No external account is needed to add this guidance.
entries.plain_when: Useful for projects explicitly building finance, accounting, tax or bookkeeping features. Money uncertainty alone is not enough.
entries.summary: Self-contained finance and bookkeeping guidance: exact currency arithmetic, source trails, data quality, account isolation and specialist review.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project touches money (detected stripe / plaid / a payments or tax surface).
entries.verified_against: first-party self-contained customer reference; local audience and installed-reference audit
entries.notes: First-party. Copied as a reference document (never into a native autoload directory such as .claude/rules/). /setup skips it when the target already exists.

entries.name: Webhook handling rule pack
entries.plain_summary: Help Claude handle updates from services, such as payment notifications, without trusting fakes or processing the same update twice.
entries.plain_access: Adds a local reference document. It does not itself connect to a service or process incoming updates.
entries.plain_account: No external account is needed to add this guidance.
entries.plain_when: Useful when your app receives updates from another service, such as payment notifications.
entries.summary: Self-contained service-notification guidance: signature verification, durable acceptance, safe retries, replay authorization and outgoing destination checks.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project receives webhooks (detected stripe / svix / a webhook route).
entries.verified_against: first-party self-contained customer reference; local audience and installed-reference audit
entries.notes: First-party. Pairs with the Stripe MCP entry. Copied as a reference document, never into a native autoload directory such as .claude/rules/.

entries.plain_summary: Give Claude instructions for choosing useful tests and checking that changes work.

entries.plain_account: No external account is needed to add this guidance.
entries.plain_when: Useful when your project already has tests or you choose help with checking work automatically.
entries.summary: Self-contained testing guidance: useful failure examples, real-service integration evidence, account isolation and honest result boundaries.
entries.why_it_fits: Your project has a test runner (detected vitest / jest / playwright / pytest).
entries.verified_against: first-party self-contained customer reference; local audience and installed-reference audit

entries.name: Customer information and money guidance
entries.plain_name: Guidance for caring for customer information and money
entries.plain_summary: Help you plan careful handling of customer details and money without assuming you are building a finance app.
entries.plain_access: Adds a local reference document. It guides decisions; it does not connect to a service, change customer records or enforce automated protection.
entries.plain_account: No external account is needed to add this guidance.
entries.plain_when: Useful when the project handles customer details or money, or when those needs are uncertain. Includes non-software businesses.
entries.summary: Self-contained protective guidance for data minimization, customer access, payment collection, consent, backups and honest evidence.
entries.why_it_fits: Your answers indicate money or personal information, separate customer records, or uncertainty requiring protective guidance.
entries.verified_against: first-party self-contained customer reference; local audience and installed-reference audit
entries.notes: Protective guidance only. Does not establish compliance, financial correctness or product safety. Copy only after review and approval; skip customized existing targets.
